name: Knoxville
tagline: Gateway to the Smokies, University Town Energy, and No State Income Tax
description: Knoxville is a hidden gem for FIRE seekers who want affordable living, stunning natural beauty, and the cultural energy of a major university town. Nestled at the doorstep of Great Smoky Mountains National Park -- America's most visited national park -- Knoxville offers four distinct seasons, a revitalized downtown with excellent restaurants and breweries, and Tennessee's zero state income tax on earned income. Housing costs remain remarkably low for a city of its quality, making your nest egg stretch further than almost anywhere in the eastern United States.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – safe university district and suburbs, typical downtown caution
quickFacts.climate: Humid subtropical with warm summers and cool, mild winters

housing.description: Cheapest-acceptable studio or older 1BR in North Knoxville or a value pocket near the university

dining.description: Casual Market Square meat-and-threes a few times a week; mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: ACA marketplace Silver plan on the TN federal marketplace, subsidized if MAGI is kept under the 2026 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600 single); assumes an early retiree (45–55) — above the cliff, premium tax credits vanish and this line climbs toward ~$1,000/mo

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance and gas; a car is needed for Smokies access (TN premiums are cheap)

entertainment.description: Free hiking in the Smokies, Ijams Nature Center, Market Square events, budget UT tickets

1M.lifestyle: A cheapest-acceptable studio or older one-bedroom in North Knoxville or a value pocket near the university, with home cooking the norm and casual Market Square meat-and-threes a few times a week. Great Smoky Mountains National Park charges no entrance fee, so weekend hiking costs little beyond gas, and a paid-off car handles the drive. The ACA Silver premium stays affordable only if MAGI is managed under the 2026 ~$62,600 cliff, and healthcare plus the car form a hard cost floor. Tennessee's zero income tax on withdrawals stretches every dollar in one of the more affordable cities in the eastern US.

housing.description: A decent 1BR in Bearden or a renovated condo in the Old City

dining.description: Dining out several times a week at downtown spots like OliBea and The Plaid Apron

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost stays low only if MAGI is managed under the ~$62,600 cliff

transportation.description: A reliable car with full coverage and maintenance for regular Smokies excursions

entertainment.description: UT Vols season tickets, Knoxville Symphony, brewery tours, fly-fishing trips

2M.lifestyle: A decent one-bedroom in Bearden or a renovated Old City space, dining out several times a week at spots like OliBea and The Plaid Apron, and a reliable car for regular Smokies trips. UT Vols games, Knoxville Symphony concerts, and Saturday farmers markets fill the calendar, with a Silver plan kept affordable if MAGI stays under the cliff. The low cost base and university-town energy make for comfortable, well-rounded living with real monthly margin.

housing.description: A high-quality 1BR or small home in Sequoyah Hills or Farragut, some near Fort Loudoun Lake

dining.description: Regular fine dining at J.C. Holdway, The Lonesome Dove, and Kaizen; wine dinners

healthcare.description: A Gold-tier plan (UT Medical Center network); padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff where premium tax credits phase out

transportation.description: A late-model SUV for mountain adventures, premium insurance

entertainment.description: Premium UT football tickets, a Big Ears Festival weekend, private fly-fishing guides

3M.lifestyle: A high-quality one-bedroom or small home in Sequoyah Hills or Farragut, some near Fort Loudoun Lake, with regular dinners at J.C. Holdway and The Lonesome Dove. A late-model SUV handles mountain roads, healthcare is a Gold plan padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff, and there is room for premium UT football tickets, guided fly-fishing, and a Big Ears Festival weekend each spring. Knoxville's low costs leave genuine margin each month for travel and giving.

housing.description: A luxury lakefront home on Fort Loudoun Lake with a dock, or a historic Sequoyah Hills home

dining.description: Fine dining several nights a week plus a private chef for entertaining and Blackberry Farm dining

healthcare.description: An unsubsidized Gold/Platinum plan plus concierge medicine and executive health screenings

transportation.description: A luxury SUV plus a boat on the lake, premium insurance, detailing

entertainment.description: UT skybox access, Blackberry Farm overnight stays, guided Smokies experiences, arts patronage

domesticHelp.description: Weekly deep cleaning, landscaping, and dock maintenance

luxuryExtras.description: Regular Blackberry Farm retreats, quarterly travel, wine collecting, university philanthropy

5M.lifestyle: A luxury lakefront home on Fort Loudoun Lake with a dock, weekly housekeeping, and concierge-level care on an unsubsidized premium plan. The city's best restaurants become a several-nights-a-week habit, a luxury SUV and a boat cover recreation, and Blackberry Farm overnight stays are within reach. Business-class flights from McGhee Tyson and regular travel fit comfortably. Knoxville's affordability and zero state income tax leave substantial margin at this level.

housing.description: A trophy lakefront estate on Tellico or Fort Loudoun Lake with a private dock, or a historic West Knoxville compound

dining.description: A private chef several days a week, catered events, exclusive Blackberry Farm wine dinners

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized concierge practice plus specialist access at Vanderbilt a short drive away — fully out of subsidy range

transportation.description: A premium vehicle plus car service, with boat-club outings on the lake

entertainment.description: Club-level UT season tickets at Neyland Stadium, national-park conservation funding, international travel

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeping several days a week plus dock and grounds service

luxuryExtras.description: Regular Blackberry Farm getaways, first-class travel, Smoky Mountain conservation philanthropy, art collecting

10M.lifestyle: A trophy lakefront estate on Tellico or Fort Loudoun Lake, housekeeping several days a week with dock and grounds service, and a private chef several days a week, with concierge medicine and specialist access at Vanderbilt a short drive away. Travel is first class, a premium vehicle and car service handle the roads, boat-club outings cover the lake, and club-level UT season tickets keep fall Saturdays at Neyland Stadium. In a metro this affordable, roughly $189k a year funds an uncapped, well-supported life with room for major university and Smokies-conservation philanthropy.
